messages:
jordan: Quick heads-up — I want to start a long-lived refactor to reduce cross-service coupling in the runtime control plane. Not a full extract; thinking 'service tiling' along capability corridors. Goal: pay down tech debt and make ownership clearer. Anyone up for a short sync tomorrow?

sasha: sounds good. can you frame the initial scope? which hotpaths are in/out?

kevin: main targets: session routing, tenant-metadata enrichment, and the KV cache ownership overlap. The trick is to avoid perf regressions on the hotpath (token loop).

aria: we should land a compatibility contract before any cutover. propose a thin facade with a version header to gradually migrate traffic.

kevin: +1. propose header: X-Runtime-Surface: v1|v2 and keep payload stable. We can add opt-in flags for new behavior.

sasha: what about batching semantics when requests cross tile boundaries? we can't lose batching efficiency.

kevin: two options: keep internal batch coordinator in the facade (cheaper rollout, more coupling) or forward raw requests to the tiled service and build a batching adapter there. tradeoffs: rollout complexity vs performance isolation.

jordan: proposal: create a "tiling-gateway" — a thin router + feature-flag layer. Migrate tenants incrementally by header/flag. Rollout plan: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 3 weeks with automated rollbacks on SLO breaches.

aria: acceptance criteria suggestion: no >5% increase in p95 latency on the hotpath, cost neutral within two weeks post-cutover, and zero schema changes to downstream telemetry events.

sasha: operational note — we need per-tenant telemetry to attribute cost/latency deltas. Redwood Console should show delta per rollout and model.

kevin: I'll sketch the interface. initial request shape (keep minimal):
```json
{
  "path": "/v1/generate",
  "tenant": "t-123",
  "model": "redwood/llama-3x",
  "input": "...",
  "headers": {
    "X-Runtime-Surface": "v2"
  }
}
```

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: staging -> tomorrow 02:00 UTC (canary gate toggles enabled).

jordan: owners: sasha will own the tiling-gateway service. kevin + aria will pair on interface, tests, and perf benchmarks. I'll write an RFC draft and ops runbook.

sasha: also need operator handover doc and a rollback plan. set canary to auto-fail if error rate >1% or p95 regresses >5%.

aria: :thumbsup: we'll add a quality regression suite that diffs outputs on canonical prompts and flags semantic drift.

jordan: actions: 1) RFC draft by EOD Fri (me) 2) Interface sketch PR by Mon (kevin) 3) Staging deploy slot booked (deploy-bot). Thanks — will post RFC link here when ready.

sasha: thanks all. will start a checklist and add owners to the board.

kevin: linking to a small perf spike note in the thread once I have microbenchmarks.

deploy-bot: note: remember to tag the deploy with "tiling-gateway" and include linking issue.
